note: Ships inside the app as the offline fallback. Host an identical-shape copy on a free static host so the app can fetch newer versions without an app-store update. Watering intervals are baseline averages for an indoor plant in moderate light at room temperature.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top 2-3 cm of soil dry out, then water thoroughly until it drains.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid (10-10-10) at half strength in spring/summer.
commonMistakes: Overwatering — soggy soil rots the roots.
Using a pot with no drainage holes.
species.propagation: Very easy. Cut a 10-15 cm stem just below a node (the bump where a leaf meets the stem), put it in water, and roots appear in 2-4 weeks. Pot up once roots are a few cm long.

species.waterHowTo: Let soil dry completely between waterings; water less in winter.
species.light: Low to bright indirect; tolerates almost anything.
species.fertilizer: Cactus/succulent feed, diluted, in growing season only.
commonMistakes: Overwatering — the #1 killer.
Watering on a fixed schedule instead of checking the soil.
species.propagation: Division keeps the yellow edges; leaf sections (10cm, right way up, in barely-moist mix) root in 1-2 months but come back plain green.

species.waterHowTo: Allow soil to dry out fully; its rhizomes store water.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season only.
commonMistakes: Overwatering causes yellowing and rot.
Assuming yellow leaves mean it needs more water (usually the opposite).
species.propagation: Division of the potato-like rhizomes is fastest. Single leaves in moist mix DO work but take 3-6 months to grow a tiny rhizome — set them and forget them.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top 2-3 cm is dry; let excess drain.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength in spring/summer.
commonMistakes: Too little light means no leaf splits.
Soggy soil leads to root rot.
species.propagation: Stem cutting WITH a node (the knuckle where aerial roots emerge) — a leaf alone will never root. Water-root 3-6 weeks until roots hit 5cm, then pot. Spring cuttings root fastest.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let the top of the soil dry slightly.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, spring/summer.
commonMistakes: Tap-water fluoride browns leaf tips — use filtered water.
Letting it dry out completely.
species.propagation: Pot the dangling plantlets while STILL attached to mama; cut the runner a couple of weeks later once they root. Nearly foolproof.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist; it dramatically droops when thirsty, then recovers.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Direct sun scorches leaves.
Chronic underwatering until it droops every time.
species.propagation: Division only: unpot, tease the crowns apart so each clump keeps roots and leaves, repot. No cuttings possible.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top 3-4 cm is dry; keep consistent.
species.fertilizer: High-nitrogen or balanced feed in growing season.
commonMistakes: Moving it around — it hates change and drops leaves.
Inconsistent watering.
species.propagation: Tip cutting with 1-2 leaves; rinse until the milky sap stops, then root in water (4-8 weeks). For thick trunks, air-layering is the sure bet.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top few cm dry; water less in winter.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, spring/summer.
commonMistakes: Overwatering drops the lower leaves.
Dusty leaves block light — wipe them.
species.propagation: Tip cuttings (rinse the sap) in water or moist soil; air-layer thick stems. Wear gloves — the latex irritates.

species.waterHowTo: Soak thoroughly, then let soil dry out completely.
species.fertilizer: Cactus/succulent feed, diluted, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering — leaves go mushy.
Not enough light makes it leggy and pale.
species.propagation: Pups only: separate offsets at about a fifth of the parent's size, with their own roots, and pot in gritty mix. Aloe LEAF cuttings just rot — don't bother.

species.waterHowTo: Water deeply, then let dry out fully.
species.fertilizer: Succulent feed, diluted, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering causes leaf drop and rot.
Too little light leads to weak, stretched growth.
species.propagation: Single leaves callused 3 days root on dry mix in a few weeks, but stem cuttings (also callused) make a real tree far faster.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top 2-3 cm is dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
Leggy growth from too little light.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings root readily in water — snip below a node and submerge it; pot up after a couple of weeks.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top few cm dry; leaves droop slightly when thirsty.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Not rotating it — it leans toward light.
Overwatering.
species.propagation: Famous for babies: little pups pop up in the soil and on the stem. Cut a pup off with roots and pot it — that's why it's the 'sharing plant'.

species.waterHowTo: Keep consistently moist, never soggy or bone dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
species.humidity: High — loves a bathroom or regular misting.
commonMistakes: Letting it dry out — fronds crisp fast.
Low humidity causes leaf drop.
species.propagation: Division of the root ball in spring, or pot up the fuzzy runners it sends out. Spores work but take a year of patience.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist with filtered or rain water.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at quarter-to-half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Tap water browns the edges — use filtered/rain water.
Low humidity and direct sun crisp the leaves.
species.propagation: Division only, in spring while repotting — cuttings can't root. Keep new divisions extra humid for 2 weeks.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let the top dry slightly between waterings.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Spider mites in dry air — check leaf undersides.
Letting it dry out fully.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings root easily in water or soil — take a 10 cm tip and pot it once roots form.

species.waterHowTo: Let top half of soil dry; sensitive to overwatering.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Fluoride/salts in tap water brown the tips — use filtered water.
Overwatering.
species.propagation: Cane cuttings: cut a stem section, remember which way is up, stand it in water or moist soil. The beheaded parent resprouts below the cut with multiple heads.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let the top dry slightly.
species.light: Bright light; some direct sun keeps colors vivid.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Drops leaves when moved or in a draft.
Low light dulls the colors.
species.propagation: Stem-tip cuttings root in warm, humid conditions. Dip in rooting hormone and keep covered. Sap is irritating — wear gloves.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top 3-4 cm is dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid, growing season.
commonMistakes: Too little light means it won't grow large.
Leaf splitting is normal, not a problem.
species.propagation: Division of offsets at repotting time — home propagation from cuttings isn't possible; commercial plants come from seed or division.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let the top dry slightly. Use filtered water.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Tap water browns the tips.
Overwatering causes root rot.
species.propagation: By division of the clumping stems, or from seed. Most home growers split a congested clump at repotting.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top 2-3 cm is dry; sensitive to overwatering.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
Direct sun scorches the fronds.
species.propagation: Only from seed — it can't be rooted from cuttings. Nurseries plant several seedlings per pot for a full look.

species.waterHowTo: Water from the bottom with room-temp water; keep leaves dry.
species.fertilizer: African violet feed, diluted, regularly while blooming.
commonMistakes: Cold water or water on the leaves causes spots.
Too little light stops blooming.
species.propagation: A healthy leaf with 2-3cm of stem, set at 45° in moist mix; babies appear at the base in 6-10 weeks. Water-rooting works too but soil transition is gentler this way.

species.waterHowTo: Water the bark/moss thoroughly once a week; never let roots sit in water.
species.fertilizer: Orchid feed, weakly, weekly during growth.
commonMistakes: Watering into the crown rots it.
Potting in regular soil instead of orchid bark.
species.propagation: Not from cuttings. Wait for a keiki (a baby on the flower spike) to grow 2-3 roots of 5cm+, then cut it off and pot in bark. Multi-crown plants can be divided; that's it.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top few cm dry; it's a jungle cactus, not a desert one.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, after blooming.
commonMistakes: Treating it like a desert cactus and underwatering.
Moving it while budding causes bud drop.
species.propagation: Very easy: twist off a Y-shaped piece of 2-3 segments, let it callous a day or two, then push into moist soil.

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry out completely. Water the soil, not the rosette.
species.fertilizer: Succulent feed, diluted, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots the center.
Stretching and pale color from too little light.
species.propagation: Twist a full leaf off cleanly, let it callus 3-5 days, lay it ON dry gritty mix and wait — mist lightly only after roots and a baby rosette show (2-4 weeks). Or behead a leggy plant and re-root the crown.

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry out fully; water sparingly in winter.
species.light: Bright indirect to some direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Succulent feed, diluted, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
Too much harsh direct sun can scorch it.
species.propagation: By offsets — pull off the small pups that cluster at the base, each with a few roots, and pot in cactus mix.

species.waterHowTo: Water when soil is dry; shriveled pearls mean it's thirsty.
species.fertilizer: Succulent feed, diluted, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering causes mushy, bursting pearls.
Too little light makes sparse strands.
species.propagation: Lay a strand on top of moist gritty mix; it roots at every node touching soil in 2-4 weeks. Far more reliable than dangling cuttings in water.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let the top dry slightly.
species.fertilizer: High-phosphorus feed, diluted, to encourage blooms.
commonMistakes: Low humidity stops blooming.
Overwatering rots the roots.
species.propagation: By division — separate offshoots with their own roots — or by stem cuttings that already have aerial roots.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top 2-3 cm is dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Cold drafts cause leaf drop.
Sap is irritating — wash hands after handling.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings — cut the cane into sections each with a node, lay or stand in moist soil. Wear gloves; the sap is an irritant.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top few cm dry; tolerant of occasional neglect.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Cold below 15°C damages it.
Overwatering in low light.
species.propagation: By division at repotting, or by stem cuttings rooted in water. Choose stems with a few leaves.

species.waterHowTo: Keep consistently moist; it faints dramatically when dry, then revives.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at quarter strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Drying out — it collapses fast.
Low humidity crisps the leaves.
species.propagation: Stem-tip cuttings root easily in water or moist soil; keep them humid (a covered tray) and new growth appears quickly.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top half of the soil dry; very forgiving.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering (almost the only way to harm it).
Direct sun scorches the leaves.
species.propagation: Division of rhizome clumps, each piece with 2-3 leaves. Slow to resettle — be patient the first months.

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry out completely; its swollen base stores water.
species.fertilizer: Cactus/succulent feed, diluted, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering — it's basically a succulent.
Pot too large holds too much moisture.
species.propagation: By offsets — mature plants sprout pups at the base that can be cut off with roots and potted. Otherwise grown from seed.

species.waterHowTo: Let soil dry most of the way; the thick leaves store water.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Cutting off the bloom spurs — flowers regrow from them.
Overwatering.
species.propagation: Node cutting with 1-2 leaves, in water or sphagnum; roots in 3-6 weeks. Never remove the old leafless flower spurs — next year's blooms come from exactly there.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; water the soil, keep leaves dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Water on the leaves causes mildew.
Soggy soil rots the rhizome.
species.propagation: The party trick: pin a whole leaf flat on moist mix and nick the big veins — plantlets sprout from every cut. Keep covered and humid.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top 2-3 cm is dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Leggy, sparse growth from too little light.
Overwatering drops leaves.
species.propagation: Stem-tip cuttings rooted in soil (use rooting hormone), or air-layering for larger plants.

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry out well; very drought tolerant.
species.light: Bright light, direct sun is fine.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering causes trunk rot.
Too little light weakens it.
species.propagation: By cane cuttings or offsets. Cut a section of trunk/cane and root it in soil; pups at the base can also be detached.

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry out fully between waterings.
species.fertilizer: Succulent or balanced feed, diluted, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots the base.
Needs long dark nights in autumn to rebloom.
species.propagation: Stem or leaf cuttings; let them callous, then set in dry soil. Roots and new shoots form readily.

species.waterHowTo: Soak in water for 20-30 min weekly, then shake off and dry upside down.
species.fertilizer: Bromeliad/air-plant feed in the soak water, monthly.
commonMistakes: Leaving water trapped in the base rots it.
Never watering because it's an 'air' plant.
species.propagation: Pups appear at the base after flowering; separate them at a third of the parent's size. No soil at any point — ever.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top few cm dry; let it drain fully.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering causes yellow leaves and rot.
Moving it often causes leaf drop.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings 15-20 cm long, rooted in water or soil in warm conditions. Take them in spring/summer for best success.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; don't let it dry out fully.
species.light: Bright indirect to some direct light.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Dry air and drying out brown the needles.
Low light causes droopy, sparse branches.
species.propagation: Hard at home — practically only from seed. Cuttings rarely root and lose the symmetrical shape.

species.waterHowTo: Keep consistently moist; wilts quickly when dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Drying out causes sudden wilting.
Low light fades the colorful spots.
species.propagation: Stem-tip cuttings root in water within a week or two — very easy. Pinch tips to keep it bushy.

species.waterHowTo: Water when top 2-3 cm is dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Low humidity slows growth and browns edges.
Overwatering.
species.propagation: Node cuttings root fast in water (2-3 weeks). Always include a node — leaf-only cuttings are decoration.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; mist in dry air.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Yellowing and needle drop from dry air.
It has hidden thorns — handle with care.
species.propagation: By division of the tuberous roots at repotting. Cut the clump into sections that each have stems and roots.

species.waterHowTo: In water, change it weekly with filtered/distilled water; in soil, keep moist.
species.fertilizer: Very dilute feed, occasionally.
commonMistakes: Tap-water chlorine/fluoride yellows it — use filtered water.
Direct sun scorches it.
species.propagation: Cut a stalk section below a node, root it in fresh water (change weekly). The cut parent sprouts new shoots below the cut.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; don't let it dry out fully.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Drying out browns the leaf edges.
Direct midday sun scorches leaves.
species.propagation: From fresh seed (green coffee 'cherries') or semi-hardwood stem cuttings. Cuttings are slow but keep the parent's traits.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let the top dry slightly.
species.light: Bright indirect light keeps the purple stripes vivid.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Fading color in low light.
Gets leggy — pinch tips to keep it full.
species.propagation: Almost too easy: snip a few cm of stem and pop it in water or straight into soil; roots in days.

species.waterHowTo: Keep consistently moist; wilts fast when dry.
species.light: Bright indirect; some morning sun deepens color.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Letting it dry out and collapse.
Letting it flower — pinch buds to keep leaves lush.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings root in water in under a week. Pinch tips often for a bushy plant.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top half dry; the thick leaves store water.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering — it rots easily.
Too little light makes it leggy.
species.propagation: Leaf or stem cuttings root readily in water or soil. A single leaf with a bit of stalk will sprout a new plant.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top half of the soil dry between waterings.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering causes limp stems.
Harsh sun fades the markings.
species.propagation: Leaf cuttings: cut a leaf with its stalk, or cut a leaf in half across the veins, and set in moist soil — babies form at the base.

species.waterHowTo: Let dry out between waterings; soft, flat leaves mean thirsty.
species.fertilizer: Succulent feed, diluted, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots the thin stems.
Too little light spaces the hearts far apart.
species.propagation: Lay strands on soil so the little tubers ('beads') along the vine touch the surface, or root stem cuttings in water.

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry out fully; very drought tolerant.
species.fertilizer: Succulent feed, diluted, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
Beads drop off at the lightest touch — handle gently.
species.propagation: From the plump leaves that fall off: let them callous, lay on dry soil, and each sprouts a new plantlet.

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry out completely; water rarely in winter.
species.fertilizer: Cactus feed, diluted, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering causes rot.
The fuzzy dots are tiny barbed spines — handle with tongs.
species.propagation: Twist off a pad, let the cut callous for several days, then set it upright in dry cactus mix. Use tongs to avoid the spines.

species.waterHowTo: Soak when fully dry; almost no water in winter.
species.fertilizer: Cactus feed, diluted, in summer only.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots it from the base.
Too little light dulls and elongates it.
species.propagation: Usually only from seed (it rarely offsets). Seed is slow but reliable in warm, bright conditions.

species.waterHowTo: Keep a little water in the central cup; flush and refill weekly. Keep soil barely moist.
species.fertilizer: Very dilute feed in the soil, sparingly.
commonMistakes: Stagnant water in the cup goes foul — flush it.
The main plant dies after flowering (normal).
species.propagation: The mother blooms once, then spends herself making pups. Cut pups off at a third of her size and pot them; the fading mother is normal, not your fault.

species.waterHowTo: Soak the root ball/mount in water weekly, then let it drain and nearly dry.
species.fertilizer: Dilute feed added to the soak water, monthly in summer.
commonMistakes: Letting the flat 'shield' fronds rot from constant wet.
Too little humidity.
species.propagation: Pups appear at the base — slice one off with some roots and shield fronds and mount it on wood over damp sphagnum.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist; water the soil around the rosette, not into the center.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at quarter strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Water pooling in the central 'nest' rots the crown.
Dry air crisps the fronds.
species.propagation: By spores only (the brown lines under mature fronds) — slow and tricky at home. It does not divide like clumping ferns.

species.waterHowTo: Never let it dry out — keep consistently moist with filtered water.
species.light: Medium indirect light, no direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Very dilute feed, growing season.
commonMistakes: One dry-out and the delicate fronds crisp.
Low humidity and drafts.
species.propagation: By division of the clump at repotting — separate sections each with roots and fronds. Keep divisions very humid.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top few cm are dry; let it drain well.
species.light: Medium to bright indirect light; tolerates lower light.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering causes root rot.
Tap-water salts brown the tips.
species.propagation: From seed only, which is very slow. Multiple seedlings are potted together for fullness; it can't be rooted from cuttings.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist — it likes more water than most palms — but not waterlogged.
species.light: Bright indirect to some direct light.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Dry air and dry soil brown the fronds.
Too little light causes weak, floppy growth.
species.propagation: From seed only. Like most palms it can't be propagated from cuttings or division at home.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top half is dry; it dislikes soggy soil.
species.fertilizer: Palm or balanced feed, diluted, in summer.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots the crown.
Very toxic if eaten — keep away from pets and kids.
species.propagation: By offsets ('pups') that form on the trunk or at the base — remove one, let it callous, and pot it. Slow to establish.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top 2-3 cm is dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Too little light fades the white pinstripes.
Overwatering.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings with a node root in water or soil. It can also be divided when it forms multiple growth points.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top 2-3 cm is dry.
species.light: Bright indirect light — needed to keep the pink variegation.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Too little light reverts it to all green.
Letting fully-pink leaves stay — they can't photosynthesize.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings with a node; choose a cutting with both green and pink for a balanced new plant. Roots in water or moss.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top few cm are dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
Gets viny — pinch to keep compact, or give it a pole to climb.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings with a node root quickly in water — one of the easiest aroids to propagate.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let only the very top dry. Use filtered water.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Low humidity and dry soil cause browning and drop.
It may go dormant in winter — don't assume it's dead.
species.propagation: By division of the underground rhizome/corms ('cormlets'). Separate offsets with roots and pot them; it can't be done from leaf cuttings.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist during the growing season.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength while in leaf.
commonMistakes: Expecting winter leaves — it dies back to a dormant tuber, which is normal.
Cold below 15°C harms it.
species.propagation: By dividing the tubers when dormant. Cut a tuber so each piece has an 'eye' (bud), let it dry a day, then replant in spring.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top 2-3 cm is dry; keep leaves dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Water on leaves causes powdery mildew.
Soggy soil rots the cane base.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings with a node root easily in water — it's a cane begonia, so cut between joints and root the piece.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top few cm are dry; the leaves fold up at night.
species.light: Bright indirect to some direct light.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Thinking it's dead during dormancy — it rests, then regrows from the bulbs.
Overwatering the bulbs.
species.propagation: By dividing the small bulbs ('bulbils') in the soil. Separate a handful and replant a few cm deep — they multiply fast.

species.waterHowTo: Water from the bottom when the top feels dry; keep water off the crown.
species.fertilizer: Low-nitrogen feed, diluted, while in bloom.
commonMistakes: Warm rooms make it wilt and go dormant early.
Water on the tuber crown causes rot.
species.propagation: From seed, or by carefully cutting the tuber into pieces each with a growth point — though tuber division often fails, so seed is more reliable.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist with filtered/rain water; it likes acidic soil.
species.light: Bright light with some direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Acid-loving (ericaceous) feed, diluted, in growing season.
commonMistakes: Bud drop from changes in light, temperature, or watering.
Alkaline tap water yellows the leaves.
species.propagation: Semi-hardwood stem cuttings in spring, with rooting hormone and bottom heat. Keep humid; rooting is slow.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist in summer; less in winter.
species.light: Bright light with several hours of direct sun.
species.fertilizer: High-potassium 'bloom' feed, regularly while flowering.
commonMistakes: Too little light means few or no flowers.
Drying out causes bud drop.
species.propagation: Softwood stem cuttings in warm weather, with rooting hormone and humidity. Takes several weeks.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top few cm are dry; deep, even watering.
species.light: As much direct sun as possible (6+ hours).
species.fertilizer: Citrus feed (extra magnesium/iron) in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Too little light — no fruit and weak growth.
Letting it swing between bone-dry and soggy causes leaf and fruit drop.
species.propagation: Semi-hardwood cuttings with rooting hormone, or air-layering. Seed-grown plants take many years to fruit and may differ from the parent.

species.waterHowTo: Keep the soil wet at all times using ONLY rain/distilled water (tray method). Tap water kills it.
species.light: Bright light with several hours of direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Never fertilize the soil — it feeds on the occasional insect.
commonMistakes: Tap or mineral water — the #1 killer.
Triggering the traps for fun wastes their energy.
It needs a cold winter dormancy.
species.propagation: Division in spring, or leaf pullings (peel a whole leaf with its white base) laid on damp sphagnum. Distilled or rain water ONLY — minerals are lethal.

species.waterHowTo: Keep the soil moist with rain/distilled water; mist to keep pitchers forming.
species.fertilizer: Don't fertilize the soil; the pitchers catch their own insects.
commonMistakes: Tap/mineral water harms it — use rain or distilled.
Low humidity stops it making pitchers.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings with a couple of nodes in damp sphagnum, kept very humid and warm. Rooting is slow.

species.waterHowTo: Living stones run on a strict calendar: water ONLY in spring and fall growth spurts, a good soak when the leaves wrinkle or feel soft (roughly every 2-4 weeks). STOP completely in summer heat dormancy, and stop all winter while the old leaf pair shrivels to feed the new one inside — some years that's only 3-5 waterings total.
species.fertilizer: Basically never — a whisper of cactus feed once in spring at most.
commonMistakes: Any water while it's splitting (the new leaves drink the old ones — extra water rots it)
Watering in winter at all
Rich soil — it wants nearly pure grit
species.propagation: From seed (slow but reliable — sow on grit, keep barely damp), or careful division of multi-headed clumps in early fall; each head keeps its own taproot section, callused a few days before replanting.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let the top dry slightly.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Gets leggy with age — pinch tips and restart from cuttings.
Overwatering.
species.propagation: Stem-tip cuttings root easily in water or soil. Take fresh cuttings every year or two to keep it looking full.

species.waterHowTo: Keep consistently moist; the tiny leaves wilt fast if it dries.
species.fertilizer: Very dilute balanced feed, growing season.
commonMistakes: Drying out browns whole patches.
Direct sun scorches the mat.
species.propagation: By division — pull off a clump with roots and press it onto moist soil. It spreads into a dense carpet on its own.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; don't let it dry out fully.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Drying out causes rapid leaf drop.
It clings and climbs — give it a surface or trim it.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings root easily in water or soil; the trailing stems also root where nodes touch moist soil.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top few cm are dry; sensitive to both extremes.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Sudden changes cause leaf drop.
Overwatering rots the woody stems.
species.propagation: Stem or tip cuttings rooted in warm, humid conditions with rooting hormone. Slow but reliable.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist in growing season; let the top dry slightly.
species.fertilizer: High-potassium 'bloom' feed, diluted, while flowering.
commonMistakes: Too little light means no goldfish-shaped blooms.
Soggy soil rots the stems.
species.propagation: Stem-tip cuttings root readily in moist soil; take several and pot together for a fuller, more floriferous plant.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top 2-3 cm is dry; reduce in winter.
species.fertilizer: High-potassium 'bloom' feed, diluted, in growing season.
commonMistakes: Too little light prevents the lipstick-tube blooms.
Cold drafts and dry air drop leaves.
species.propagation: Stem-tip cuttings 8-10 cm long root in water or soil with warmth and humidity.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top 3-4 cm is dry; keep it consistent.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, spring/summer.
commonMistakes: Drops leaves when moved or in a draft.
Overwatering and dry air both cause leaf drop.
species.propagation: Stem-tip cuttings rooted in water or moist soil; milky sap is irritating, so wash hands.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top 2-3 cm is dry; well-draining soil, never soggy.
species.light: Bright with several hours of direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Light balanced feed monthly in summer; it prefers lean soil.
commonMistakes: Soggy roots rot fast — let it dry between waterings.
Too little light indoors causes leggy growth and powdery mildew.
species.propagation: Semi-hardwood tip cuttings in summer: 10cm, strip the lower leaves, into gritty mix; roots in 4-8 weeks. Slow from seed.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top of the soil dry; the small leaves store water.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at quarter-to-half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Shallow roots rot easily — don't overwater.
Too little light fades the turtle-shell pattern.
species.propagation: Lay strands on moist soil or take stem cuttings; nodes root where they touch.

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry out well; drought-tolerant.
species.light: Bright light with some direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Diluted succulent feed, once or twice in summer.
commonMistakes: Overwatering causes rot.
Give it support — it sends out long climbing stems.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings: let the cut callous a day or two, then root in dry, gritty soil.

species.waterHowTo: Soak when fully dry; water very little in winter.
species.fertilizer: Diluted cactus feed once or twice in summer.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots the base — the #1 killer.
Needs lots of sun or it grows weak and pale.
species.propagation: Usually from seed, or offsets if it produces them. Handle with care — fine hairs hide sharp spines.

species.waterHowTo: Water when soil is dry in summer; keep nearly dry in winter.
species.light: Bright light with some direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Balanced or cactus feed monthly in the growing season.
commonMistakes: It's a climbing cactus — give it a sturdy support.
Winter overwatering rots the stems.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings: let a segment callous for several days, then plant in gritty mix.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top half dry; the thick leaves store water.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots the thin stems.
Keep water off the leaves; let the soil dry between drinks.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings root readily in water or moist soil.

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry out completely; very drought-tolerant.
species.fertilizer: Rarely — diluted succulent feed once in summer at most.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots the rosette.
Too little light makes it stretch and lose its tight shape.
species.propagation: By offsets — the 'chicks' that cluster around the parent. Detach with roots and replant.

species.waterHowTo: Water when dry; shriveled 'bananas' mean it's thirsty.
species.light: Bright indirect to some direct light.
species.fertilizer: Diluted succulent feed in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering causes mushy stems.
Too little light makes sparse strands.
species.propagation: Lay strands on soil or root stem cuttings; very easy.

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry out fully; water rarely in winter.
species.fertilizer: Diluted cactus feed once or twice in summer.
commonMistakes: The milky sap is a strong irritant — wear gloves and keep away from eyes.
Overwatering rots it.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings; let them callous well first and wear gloves — the sap is caustic.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let the top dry slightly.
species.light: Bright indirect light keeps the pink color.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Fades and gets leggy in low light — pinch tips to keep it full.
Sap can irritate skin.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings root in water within days — one of the easiest.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top 2-3 cm is dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
Leggy, small leaves in too little light.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings with a node root easily in water.

species.waterHowTo: A rainforest cactus — water when the top dries; don't let it go bone dry.
species.light: Bright indirect light, no harsh sun.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, growing season.
commonMistakes: Treating it like a desert cactus and underwatering.
Direct midday sun scorches the stems.
species.propagation: Stem-segment cuttings; let them callous briefly, then root in moist mix.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist in growth; let the top dry; it's a jungle cactus.
species.fertilizer: Balanced or bloom feed, diluted, in spring/summer.
commonMistakes: Underwatering — it's not a desert cactus.
Needs cool, dark autumn nights to flower.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings: let the cut end callous, then root in moist mix.

species.waterHowTo: Keep consistently moist; it wilts quickly when dry.
species.light: Bright with several hours of direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength every few weeks while growing.
commonMistakes: Letting it dry out and collapse.
Not pinching flowers — pinch them to keep leaves coming.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings root in water in about a week; or grow from seed.

species.waterHowTo: Keep the soil consistently moist; mint is thirsty.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength monthly in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Letting it dry out — it wilts fast.
It spreads aggressively, so keep it in its own pot.
species.propagation: Division or stem cuttings in water — extremely easy.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top few cm dry; it likes it on the dry side.
species.light: Bright with lots of direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Light feed monthly in summer; prefers lean soil.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots it.
Too little sun makes it leggy.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings or division; woody stems root slowly.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let the top dry slightly.
species.light: Bright with several hours of sun.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed at half strength monthly in summer.
commonMistakes: Letting it dry out fully.
Too little light.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings root in water; or from seed.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top dry between waterings; drought tolerant.
species.fertilizer: Light feed monthly in summer; lean soil keeps flavor strong.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
Rich soil weakens the flavor.
species.propagation: Division or stem cuttings; very easy.

species.waterHowTo: Keep consistently moist.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed at half strength monthly.
commonMistakes: Letting it dry out and bolt.
Too little light.
species.propagation: From seed (slow to germinate); doesn't root well from cuttings.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist; it bolts quickly if stressed.
species.light: Bright; some sun but not scorching heat.
species.fertilizer: Light balanced feed monthly.
commonMistakes: Heat and drying out make it bolt to seed fast.
Sow successionally for a steady supply.
species.propagation: From seed only; doesn't transplant or root well.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist.
species.fertilizer: Light feed monthly.
commonMistakes: Bolts in heat.
Tall — may need support.
species.propagation: From seed; sow where it will grow, it dislikes transplanting.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist.
species.fertilizer: Light balanced feed monthly.
commonMistakes: Toxic to cats & dogs (allium) — keep away from pets.
Snip regularly to keep it productive.
species.propagation: By division of the clump; or from seed.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top dry well; drought tolerant once established.
species.fertilizer: Light feed monthly in summer.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots it.
Poor airflow invites mildew.
species.propagation: Softwood cuttings in summer; or layering.

species.waterHowTo: Water deeply then let dry out; hates wet feet.
species.fertilizer: Very little; lean, gritty soil is best.
commonMistakes: Overwatering and rich soil kill it.
Needs excellent drainage and airflow.
species.propagation: Semi-hardwood cuttings in summer, in gritty mix — it will NOT root from old bare wood, so take tips with some green.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; wilts when dry.
species.fertilizer: Light balanced feed monthly.
commonMistakes: Spreads vigorously — contain it.
Drying out.
species.propagation: Division or stem cuttings; very easy.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top dry; dislikes soggy soil.
species.fertilizer: Light feed monthly in summer.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
French tarragon can't be grown from seed — use cuttings/division.
species.propagation: Division or cuttings (French type is sterile).

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top few cm are dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed at half strength in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
Slow-growing — be patient.
species.propagation: Semi-hardwood cuttings (slow) or layering.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; let the top dry slightly.
species.fertilizer: Little needed; light feed monthly at most.
commonMistakes: Overfeeding reduces flowers.
Overwatering.
species.propagation: From seed; self-sows readily.

species.waterHowTo: Keep consistently moist; it's thirsty.
species.fertilizer: Nitrogen-rich feed monthly in summer.
commonMistakes: Letting it dry out.
Cold below 10°C damages it.
species.propagation: Division, or root a fresh stalk in water.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top dry between waterings.
species.fertilizer: Light feed monthly.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
Cats may flatten it — protect young plants.
species.propagation: Division, cuttings, or seed.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top dry slightly.
species.fertilizer: Light feed monthly; lean soil is fine.
commonMistakes: Overwatering.
Too little sun.
species.propagation: From seed.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed monthly.
commonMistakes: Bolts if stressed or dry.
Plant away from dill (they cross).
species.propagation: From seed; dislikes transplanting.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; shallow roots dry fast.
species.fertilizer: Low-nitrogen balanced feed monthly.
commonMistakes: Letting it dry out.
Cold sensitive.
species.propagation: Stem cuttings root in water; seed is unreliable.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist; deep, regular watering. Never let it wilt then flood.
species.fertilizer: Tomato feed (high potassium) every 1-2 weeks once fruiting.
commonMistakes: Uneven watering causes blossom-end rot and splitting.
Foliage is toxic to pets.
species.propagation: From seed; side-shoots ('suckers') also root easily in water.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist; let the top just dry.
species.fertilizer: Tomato/pepper feed every 1-2 weeks when fruiting.
commonMistakes: Overwatering drops flowers.
Foliage toxic to pets.
species.propagation: From seed; needs warmth to germinate.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist.
species.fertilizer: Tomato/pepper feed every 1-2 weeks when fruiting.
commonMistakes: Inconsistent watering causes blossom-end rot.
Foliage toxic to pets.
species.propagation: From seed.

species.waterHowTo: Water deeply and often; very thirsty in fruiting.
species.fertilizer: Balanced then high-potassium feed when fruiting.
commonMistakes: Drying out makes bitter fruit.
Give it a trellis to climb.
species.propagation: From seed; sensitive to transplant.

species.waterHowTo: Water deeply at the base; keep leaves dry.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed, then high-potassium when fruiting.
commonMistakes: Wet leaves get powdery mildew.
It gets big — give it space.
species.propagation: From seed.

species.waterHowTo: Keep consistently moist; shallow roots dry fast.
species.light: Bright; part sun, dislikes intense heat.
species.fertilizer: Light nitrogen feed every couple of weeks.
commonMistakes: Heat and dryness make it bolt and turn bitter.
Harvest outer leaves for a longer crop.
species.propagation: From seed; regrows from the base after cutting.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist.
species.fertilizer: Nitrogen-rich feed every couple of weeks.
commonMistakes: Bolts fast in heat and long days.
Sow in cool weather.
species.propagation: From seed.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist.
species.fertilizer: Nitrogen-rich feed every few weeks.
commonMistakes: Watch for cabbage caterpillars.
Sweeter after a light frost.
species.propagation: From seed.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed every few weeks.
commonMistakes: Letting it dry out.
Harvest outer stalks to keep it going.
species.propagation: From seed.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist for even roots.
species.fertilizer: Low-nitrogen; too much makes forked roots.
commonMistakes: Stony or heavy soil forks the roots.
Uneven watering splits them.
species.propagation: From seed, sown directly; doesn't transplant.

species.waterHowTo: Keep consistently moist for fast, mild roots.
species.fertilizer: Little needed; too much nitrogen means all leaf.
commonMistakes: Heat and dryness make them woody and hot.
Sow thinly so roots can size up.
species.propagation: From seed; ready in weeks.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist, especially when flowering and podding.
species.fertilizer: Low-nitrogen; beans make their own.
commonMistakes: Dry spells drop the flowers.
Pick often to keep them producing.
species.propagation: From seed, sown directly.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist while flowering and podding.
species.light: Full to part sun; likes cool weather.
species.fertilizer: Low-nitrogen; peas fix their own.
commonMistakes: Heat stops them cropping — grow in cool seasons.
Give them something to climb.
species.propagation: From seed, sown directly.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist; water the soil, keep fruit dry.
species.fertilizer: High-potassium feed every 1-2 weeks when flowering/fruiting.
commonMistakes: Wet fruit and crowns rot — mulch and airflow help.
Net against birds.
species.propagation: Peg the runners into little pots of soil while still attached; cut the umbilical once they root (2-3 weeks).

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist with rain/filtered water; it needs acidic soil.
species.fertilizer: Ericaceous (acid-loving) feed in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Alkaline soil/tap water yellows the leaves.
Grow two varieties for better fruit.
species.propagation: Softwood or hardwood cuttings; slow.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist; deep watering.
species.fertilizer: Tomato feed every 1-2 weeks when fruiting.
commonMistakes: Cold checks it badly.
Foliage toxic to pets.
species.propagation: From seed with warmth.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist.
species.fertilizer: Light nitrogen feed monthly.
commonMistakes: Toxic to cats & dogs (allium).
Regrow from the root ends in water.
species.propagation: Stand cut root ends in water — they regrow; or from seed.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist while growing; stop watering as it matures.
species.fertilizer: Nitrogen feed in spring; stop by early summer.
commonMistakes: Toxic to cats & dogs (allium).
Too much water near harvest rots the bulbs.
species.propagation: Plant individual cloves, pointy end up, in autumn.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top is dry; avoid wetting the flowers.
species.fertilizer: Light feed monthly; too much means leaves not flowers.
commonMistakes: Deadhead spent blooms to keep it flowering.
Overwatering causes mildew.
species.propagation: From seed; very easy.

species.waterHowTo: Water deeply; big plants drink a lot.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed monthly; not too much nitrogen.
commonMistakes: Tall types need staking.
Sow directly — they dislike root disturbance.
species.propagation: From seed, sown directly.

species.waterHowTo: Water at the base when the top is dry; keep leaves dry.
species.fertilizer: Light feed monthly.
commonMistakes: Wet leaves get powdery mildew.
Deadhead for more blooms.
species.propagation: From seed; cut-and-come-again.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top is dry; tolerates some drought.
species.fertilizer: None to very little — lean soil gives more flowers.
commonMistakes: Rich soil/feeding gives all leaves, few flowers.
Watch for blackfly.
species.propagation: From seed, sown directly; edible flowers and leaves.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly moist; containers dry out fast.
species.fertilizer: High-potassium bloom feed every 1-2 weeks.
commonMistakes: Drying out in pots stops flowering.
Deadhead trailing types to keep them tidy.
species.propagation: From seed or softwood cuttings.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top dry between waterings; fairly drought tolerant.
species.fertilizer: High-potassium feed every 1-2 weeks in summer.
commonMistakes: Overwatering rots the stems.
Toxic to cats & dogs.
species.propagation: Softwood stem cuttings root very easily.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist; it likes cool, damp shade.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed monthly in spring/summer.
commonMistakes: Slugs and snails shred the leaves.
Toxic to cats & dogs.
species.propagation: By division in spring or autumn.

species.waterHowTo: Water deeply at the base 1-2× a week; keep leaves dry.
species.fertilizer: Rose feed every few weeks in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Wet foliage invites blackspot — water the soil, not the leaves.
Prune for airflow.
species.propagation: Hardwood or semi-hardwood cuttings.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist; it wilts quickly in heat, then recovers.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed in spring; soil pH changes flower color.
commonMistakes: Hot afternoon sun and dryness scorch it.
Toxic to cats & dogs.
species.propagation: Softwood cuttings in early summer.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top half of the soil is dry; it forgives a missed week far better than a soggy one.
species.light: Bright indirect; tolerates medium. More light = stronger yellow striping.
species.fertilizer: Balanced liquid at half strength, spring through summer.
commonMistakes: Overwatering in low light
Deep shade fading the variegation
species.propagation: Node cuttings root in water in 2-4 weeks — cut just below a node with 1-2 leaves.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top few centimeters dry out; heavily white leaves photosynthesize less and drink slower than green pothos.
species.light: Bright indirect keeps the marbling crisp; too dark and it greens out.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength balanced feed monthly in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Low light reverting the variegation
Watering on a fixed schedule instead of checking the soil
species.propagation: Node cuttings in water; choose stems with balanced variegation so babies keep the marble look.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top third of soil is dry; droopy chartreuse leaves are its very visible 'thirsty' signal.
species.light: Bright indirect for the loudest neon color; handles medium light.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength balanced feed monthly, spring-summer.
commonMistakes: Sunburn in direct sun
Letting it sit in a wet saucer
species.propagation: Node cuttings in water root in 2-3 weeks.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top half dries; leaves curl inward slightly when thirsty — a handy tell.
species.light: Bright indirect; silver spots dull in deep shade.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength balanced monthly in the growing season.
species.humidity: Average and up; loves a bit extra.
commonMistakes: Cold drafts spotting the leaves
Overwatering — it likes to dry out a bit
species.propagation: Node cuttings in water or moist sphagnum; roots in 3-4 weeks.

species.waterHowTo: Keep lightly, evenly moist — never soggy, never bone dry. Use distilled, filtered or rain water; tap minerals crisp the edges.
species.light: Medium indirect; direct sun bleaches the silver-striped leaves.
species.fertilizer: Quarter-strength balanced feed monthly in the growing season — it burns easily.
species.humidity: High (60%+). A humidifier or pebble tray earns you perfect leaves.
commonMistakes: Tap water crisping the edges
Low humidity curling the leaves
Letting it fully dry out
species.propagation: Division only, in spring — gently tease the root ball into clumps, each with leaves and roots. No cuttings.

species.waterHowTo: Evenly moist with filtered or rain water; the wavy leaves fold up at night (normal!) but curl tight when thirsty.
species.light: Medium to bright indirect, no direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Quarter-strength monthly, spring-summer.
species.humidity: High; brown edges = dry air or tap water.
commonMistakes: Tap water damage
Direct sun fading the pattern
species.propagation: Division only, in spring.

species.waterHowTo: Lightly moist always, filtered water preferred; the pink-splashed leaves scorch and crisp fast if it dries fully.
species.light: Bright indirect; some gentle morning sun deepens the pink.
species.fertilizer: Quarter-strength monthly in the growing season.
species.humidity: High — it's a prayer-plant cousin with the same diva habits.
commonMistakes: Dry air crisping the edges
Full sun bleaching the variegation
species.propagation: Division only — each clump needs rhizome, roots and a few leaves.

species.waterHowTo: Keep evenly moist with room-temperature filtered water; folds its leaves up nightly like praying hands.
species.light: Medium indirect; tolerates lower light better than calatheas.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength balanced monthly, spring-summer.
species.humidity: Likes it high but copes with average better than its cousins.
commonMistakes: Cold tap water shocking the roots
Direct sun fading the red veins
species.propagation: Stem cuttings with a node root readily in water (unusual for the prayer-plant family), or divide.

species.waterHowTo: Semi-succulent: water thoroughly when the pot feels light and the top half is dry. Firm coin leaves = happy; soft = thirsty.
species.fertilizer: Light feeder — half-strength monthly at most.
commonMistakes: Overwatering the succulent-ish roots
Repotting too often — it likes being snug
species.propagation: Stem or leaf cuttings in moist mix; roots in 3-5 weeks.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top half is dry; the thick teardrop leaves store water, so err dry.
species.light: Bright indirect keeps it compact and glossy.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength monthly in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Mistaking it for pilea and overwatering
Deep shade making it leggy
species.propagation: Leaf cuttings with a bit of petiole in moist mix, or stem tip cuttings in water.

species.waterHowTo: Succulent-leaved: soak, then let dry almost completely. Wrinkling hearts mean thirsty.
species.light: Bright indirect to a little direct morning sun.
species.fertilizer: Light monthly feed in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Buying a single-leaf heart and expecting a vine — without a node it stays one leaf forever
Overwatering
species.propagation: Only node cuttings make new vines; a rooted single leaf is a decoration, not a plant. Node cuttings root in sphagnum in 4-8 weeks.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the leaves lose a little gloss and the mix is dry; likes a chunky, airy mix that drains fast.
species.light: Bright indirect; a few hours of gentle sun encourages the starry bloom clusters.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength monthly while growing; a bloom-booster in spring.
commonMistakes: Cutting off the old flower spurs — blooms return on them every year
Dense soil rotting the roots
species.propagation: Node cuttings with 1-2 leaves in water or sphagnum; roots in 3-6 weeks.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top half dries; this shrubby philodendron likes brief dry spells between drinks.
species.fertilizer: Balanced half-strength monthly, spring-summer.
commonMistakes: Expecting it to climb — it clumps instead
Overpotting, which keeps soil wet too long
species.propagation: Division of the clump, or stem sections with aerial roots potted up in spring.

species.waterHowTo: Chunky orchid-bark mix, watered when the top few centimeters dry; roots must breathe or they rot.
species.light: Bright indirect; the white veins wash out in deep shade.
species.fertilizer: Quarter-strength monthly.
species.humidity: High (60%+) for those big velvet leaves.
commonMistakes: Regular potting soil suffocating the epiphytic roots
Dry air crisping leaf edges
species.propagation: Division of offsets, or stem cuttings with a node and aerial root in sphagnum.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top third dries; more forgiving than a fiddle-leaf but still hates swings between soaked and parched.
species.light: Bright indirect, a little direct sun is welcome.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed monthly in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Moving it around — ficus drop leaves when relocated
Overwatering after a leaf-drop scare
species.propagation: Tip cuttings with 1-2 leaves; rinse the milky sap, then root in water. Air-layer thick stems.

species.waterHowTo: Let the top half dry between drinks; variegated leaves drink slower than the burgundy kind.
species.light: Bright indirect keeps the cream-and-pink margins; low light reverts it to plain green.
species.fertilizer: Balanced monthly, spring-summer.
commonMistakes: Too little light for the variegation
Cold drafts causing leaf drop
species.propagation: Tip cuttings (rinse the sap) in water or soil; air-layering for thick stems.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top half dries. Sensitive to fluoride — if leaf tips brown, switch to filtered or rain water.
species.light: Medium indirect; tolerates low light slowly.
species.fertilizer: Light feeder; half-strength every 6 weeks in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Fluoridated tap water browning the tips
Overwatering in low light
species.propagation: Cane cuttings: cut a stem section, keep it right-side up, root in moist soil — the parent resprouts below the cut.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top half is dry; droopy neon striping perks up within hours of a drink.
species.light: Medium to bright indirect; too much sun bleaches the stripes.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength every 6 weeks in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Tap-water fluoride browning tips
Letting it sit soggy
species.propagation: Top or cane cuttings in water or moist soil.

species.waterHowTo: Same tank-like ZZ rules: water only when fully dry. New growth emerges lime green and matures to purple-black — that's normal.
species.light: Low to bright indirect — genuinely unfussy.
species.fertilizer: Twice a season at half strength is plenty.
commonMistakes: Watering it like a normal tropical — the rhizomes store plenty
Panicking at green new growth
species.propagation: Division of rhizomes is fastest; leaf cuttings work but take 3-6 months to sprout.

species.waterHowTo: Lightly moist in an airy mix; the zebra-striped stems store some water. It may drop leaves and semi-rest in winter — reduce water then and don't panic.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength monthly while actively growing.
species.humidity: High; spider mites attack it in dry air.
commonMistakes: Winter overwatering during its rest
Dry air inviting spider mites
species.propagation: Separate the little corms/offsets from the root ball and sprout them in moist sphagnum.

species.waterHowTo: Water when the top half dries; among the most forgiving red-leaved plants there is.
species.light: Medium indirect; brighter light = redder edges. Avoid direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength monthly in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Cold drafts below 15°C
Soggy soil in a dark corner
species.propagation: Division, or stem cuttings rooted in water.

species.waterHowTo: Evenly moist, never swampy; tidier and more drought-tolerant than a Boston fern, and happy outdoors in shade for summer.
species.light: Bright indirect indoors, shade to part shade outside.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength monthly, spring-summer.
species.humidity: Moderate-high; tougher than most ferns in normal rooms.
commonMistakes: Letting it fully dry — fronds crisp fast
Hot direct sun
species.propagation: Division of the root ball in spring.

species.waterHowTo: Keep the mix lightly moist and mist the fuzzy surface rhizomes ('feet') — but never bury them, they creep on top.
species.fertilizer: Quarter-strength monthly in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Burying the furry rhizomes and rotting them
Dry air crisping fronds
species.propagation: Cut a 'foot' (rhizome section) with a frond or two and pin it onto moist mix; it roots along its length.

species.waterHowTo: Chunky, airy mix kept lightly moist; more forgiving of a missed watering than most ferns thanks to its rhizomes.
species.light: Medium to bright indirect; even a bit of gentle sun.
species.fertilizer: Quarter-strength monthly.
species.humidity: Average and up — unusually tolerant for a fern.
commonMistakes: Watering into the central rhizome crown
Dense soil suffocating epiphytic roots
species.propagation: Divide the surface rhizomes, each with fronds attached, and lay them on fresh mix.

species.waterHowTo: Backwards from most succulents: aeoniums grow in the cool seasons and doze in summer heat — water more spring/fall, barely at all in midsummer when leaves curl closed.
species.light: Bright light with some direct sun; the rosette tips blush pink in sun.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength once or twice in the cool growing seasons.
commonMistakes: Watering hard in summer while it's dormant
Deep shade stretching the rosettes
species.propagation: Cut a rosette with 2-3cm of stem, callus 3-5 days, plant in gritty mix in the cool season.

species.waterHowTo: Soak and dry fully; thick tongue-shaped leaves rot if kept damp. Tolerates lower light than most succulents.
species.light: Bright indirect; unlike most succulents it dislikes harsh midday sun.
species.fertilizer: Once or twice a season, half strength.
commonMistakes: Full blazing sun scorching the leaves
Water sitting between the leaves
species.propagation: Pups from the base, or single leaves callused 4-5 days then set on gritty mix (slow but works).

species.waterHowTo: Soak, then let dry completely; the fuzzy silver leaves mark rot fast if splashed — water the soil, not the plant.
species.light: Bright light with some direct sun.
species.fertilizer: Sparse — a couple of feeds a season.
commonMistakes: Wetting the fuzzy leaves
Low light making it floppy
species.propagation: Leaf cuttings: callus 3-4 days, lay on dry gritty mix, wait for roots before the first tiny watering.

species.waterHowTo: Soak and dry fully; stacked square leaves wrinkle slightly when thirsty.
species.light: Bright light, some direct sun; edges blush pink with sun stress.
species.fertilizer: Rarely — twice a season.
commonMistakes: Overwatering in winter
Etiolation (stretching) in dim rooms
species.propagation: Cut a stem section, callus 2-3 days, lay or stand in gritty mix; roots at the leaf joints.

species.waterHowTo: Water deeply when fully dry in the growing season; in winter it rests — once a month at most. The white sap is irritating: gloves when handling.
species.light: Bright light with several hours of sun.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength monthly in summer only.
commonMistakes: Handling without gloves — the sap burns skin and eyes
Winter watering rotting the base
species.propagation: Cut an arm (gloves!), rinse the sap until it stops, callus 5-7 days, then plant in dry gritty mix.

species.waterHowTo: Growing season: soak when bone dry. Winter: keep it cool, bright and almost completely dry — one small drink mid-winter at most. That winter rest is what triggers the halo of spring flowers.
species.light: Full sun to very bright light.
species.fertilizer: Cactus feed monthly in summer only.
commonMistakes: Winter watering — the #1 killer
No winter cool spell, so it never blooms
species.propagation: Offsets: twist off pups, callus 3-5 days, set on gritty mix.

species.waterHowTo: Soak when fully dry spring-fall; nearly dry all winter in a cool bright spot. The reward: trumpet flowers bigger than the cactus itself.
species.fertilizer: Cactus feed monthly in summer.
commonMistakes: Skipping the cool dry winter rest (no blooms without it)
Rich soil holding too much water
species.propagation: Offsets cluster at the base — twist off, callus, replant.

species.waterHowTo: Soak when completely dry in summer; barely water in winter. Slow-growing turrets make overwatering the only real danger.
species.light: Full sun to very bright light.
species.fertilizer: A couple of cactus feeds each summer.
commonMistakes: Winter watering
Believing the glued-on paper 'flowers' some shops add are real
species.propagation: Cut a turret, callus a week, plant shallow in gritty mix.

species.waterHowTo: Water the green rootstock's soil when fully dry; go very light in winter. The neon top has no chlorophyll and lives off the graft below.
species.light: Bright indirect — NOT full sun; the colored top sunburns easily.
species.fertilizer: Rarely; a light cactus feed in summer.
commonMistakes: Full sun scorching the colored ball
Expecting it to live forever — grafts last a few years
species.propagation: The colored top makes pups that must be re-grafted onto new rootstock — a fun advanced project.

species.waterHowTo: Consistent moisture for tender, mild leaves; drought and heat turn it bitter and send it to seed.
species.light: Full sun in cool weather, part shade in summer heat.
species.fertilizer: Light nitrogen feed if leaves pale.
commonMistakes: Heat bolting — succession-sow every 2-3 weeks instead
Letting it dry out (instant bitterness)
species.propagation: Direct-sow seed every few weeks, spring and fall; sprouts in under a week.

species.waterHowTo: Even, steady moisture — stress from drought makes it bolt to flower almost overnight.
species.light: Full sun to part shade; appreciates afternoon shade in heat.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed every 3 weeks; it grows fast and hungry.
commonMistakes: Heat + dry soil = bolting
Cabbage worms — check leaf undersides
species.propagation: Seed, direct-sown in cool seasons; harvest whole heads in ~45 days or leaf-by-leaf.

species.waterHowTo: Deep, even watering — 2-3cm a week; inconsistent moisture makes loose, bitter heads. Water the soil, not the crown.
species.fertilizer: Nitrogen-rich feed until heads form, then ease off.
commonMistakes: Planting for summer harvest — it's a cool-season crop
Missing the harvest window (heads flower fast)
species.propagation: Seed started indoors 6 weeks before the last frost, or direct-sown in late summer for a fall crop.

species.waterHowTo: Steady, deep watering; sudden heavy water after drought splits the heads wide open.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed every 3 weeks while heads size up.
commonMistakes: Irregular watering splitting heads
Skipping row covers — cabbage moths find it fast
species.propagation: Seed, started indoors or direct-sown; cool-season crop for spring or fall.

species.waterHowTo: Even moisture for tender roots; drought makes them woody and cracked. Mulch helps.
species.fertilizer: Light feed; too much nitrogen grows leaves at the root's expense.
commonMistakes: Skipping thinning — each seed cluster sprouts several plants
Woody roots from erratic water
species.propagation: Direct-sow seed clusters 2-3 weeks before last frost; thin to one seedling per cluster. Greens are edible too.

species.waterHowTo: Regular water while vines establish, then it's fairly drought-tough; stop watering 2-3 weeks before harvest so tubers cure.
species.light: Full sun and heat — it loves summer.
species.fertilizer: Low nitrogen; heavy feeding grows vines instead of tubers.
commonMistakes: Planting before the soil is warm
Overfeeding nitrogen — all vine, no potato
species.propagation: From 'slips': suspend a tuber half in water, twist off the sprouts when 15cm, root them in water, plant.

species.waterHowTo: Even moisture especially while flowering (that's when tubers form); stop watering when the foliage yellows and dies back before harvest.
species.fertilizer: Balanced at planting, again when hilling; avoid fresh manure (scab).
commonMistakes: Not hilling soil over the stems — sunlit tubers turn green and toxic
Watering after die-back (rots the crop)
species.propagation: Plant certified seed potatoes (chunks with 1-2 eyes, cured a day) — not grocery-store spuds, which carry disease.

species.waterHowTo: A thirsty giant: deep watering, critical during tasseling and ear-fill. Water at the base — overhead washes pollen away.
species.fertilizer: Heavy nitrogen feeder; side-dress when knee-high and again at tasseling.
commonMistakes: Planting one long row — plant in blocks so wind pollination fills the ears
Drought during silking = gappy kernels
species.propagation: Direct-sow seed in blocks of at least 4x4 once soil is warm.

species.waterHowTo: Deep weekly soak once established — it shrugs off heat that wilts everything else. Harvest pods young, every other day.
species.fertilizer: Light balanced feed; too much nitrogen = leaves over pods.
commonMistakes: Letting pods grow big and woody — pick at finger length
Planting in cool soil (it sulks below 18°C)
species.propagation: Direct-sow seed (soak overnight first) once soil is thoroughly warm.

species.waterHowTo: Steady moisture for tender shanks; mound soil up the stems ('blanching') as they grow for more white.
species.fertilizer: Nitrogen-leaning feed every 3 weeks — long season, steady appetite.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to hill/blanch the stems
Transplant shock — trim roots and tops when transplanting instead
species.propagation: Seed started indoors in late winter; transplant pencil-thick seedlings into deep holes.

species.waterHowTo: Never let it dry — celery is ~95% water and turns stringy and bitter with any drought. The thirstiest thing in the garden.
species.fertilizer: Rich soil plus balanced feed every 3 weeks.
commonMistakes: Any dry spell = stringy stalks
Starting from seed late (it needs a long, cool season)
species.propagation: Seed (slow, 2-3 weeks to germinate), or regrow a kitchen base in water for fun greens.

species.waterHowTo: Deep drink weekly for fat stalks; mulch heavily. Established crowns tolerate dry spells but stalks get thin.
species.light: Full sun in cool climates, afternoon shade where hot.
species.fertilizer: Generous compost in spring; balanced feed after harvest.
commonMistakes: Eating the LEAVES — they're poisonous (oxalic acid); stalks only
Harvesting the first year (let crowns establish)
species.propagation: Divide crowns in early spring every 5-6 years, each piece with 2-3 buds.

species.waterHowTo: 2-3cm a week, most critical as fruit swells; drip irrigation beats overhead (wet canes invite disease).
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed in early spring; compost mulch does most of the work.
commonMistakes: Not pruning spent canes — they fruit on 2nd-year wood then die
Letting the patch wander (it will try)
species.propagation: Dig up the suckers that pop up near the row and replant — easiest fruit propagation there is.

species.waterHowTo: Deep weekly water while fruiting; established plants are tough. Mulch to keep roots cool.
species.fertilizer: Balanced spring feed.
commonMistakes: Skipping pruning — old canes crowd out the fruiting ones
Underestimating thorny varieties' ambition
species.propagation: Tip-layering: bend a cane tip to the ground, bury 5cm, and it roots by fall; cut free and move.

species.waterHowTo: Deep, infrequent watering — established vines send roots meters down; too much water = leaves instead of grapes.
species.light: Full sun on a trellis, arbor or fence.
species.fertilizer: Light spring feed only; rich soil makes rampant vine, few grapes.
commonMistakes: Timid pruning — grapes fruit on new wood; cut back HARD in late winter (up to 90%)
Overwatering/overfeeding
species.propagation: Hardwood cuttings in late winter: pencil-thick, 3 buds, two-thirds buried; roots by spring.

species.waterHowTo: Deep weekly water for in-ground trees, every few days for pots; sudden drought drops the fruit, sudden floods split it.
species.light: Full sun, the hotter the better.
species.fertilizer: Light feed — hungry figs grow leaves, not fruit.
commonMistakes: Overfeeding
Cold snaps killing potted figs — wheel them into a garage below -5°C
species.propagation: Hardwood cuttings root famously easily: 20cm winter cuttings in moist mix, warm spot, buds by spring.

species.waterHowTo: It's a bromeliad: light watering into the soil AND a splash into the leaf rosette; drains fast, hates swamp.
species.light: As much sun as you can give it.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength monthly; a foliar feed works too.
commonMistakes: Expecting quick fruit — a crown takes 2-3 years
Cold rooms (below 15°C it just stops)
species.propagation: Twist the leafy crown off a store-bought fruit, strip lower leaves, dry 2 days, root in water or soil — the classic kitchen project.

species.waterHowTo: Moist but never soggy — avocado roots rot easily; let the top few centimeters dry. Yellow leaves usually mean too much water.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength balanced monthly in the growing season.
commonMistakes: Waterlogging
Expecting fruit — seed-grown trees rarely fruit indoors; grow it for the glossy leaves
species.propagation: The toothpick trick: suspend the pit fat-end-down half in water; roots in 4-8 weeks, then pot. Pinch at 30cm for bushiness.

species.waterHowTo: A water and food monster in summer — keep evenly moist and never let the pot bake dry; ease right off in winter.
species.light: Full sun to the brightest window you own.
species.fertilizer: Feed every 2 weeks in summer; bananas are famously hungry.
species.humidity: High; brown leaf edges mean dry air.
commonMistakes: Underfeeding
Cold drafts shredding the leaves
species.propagation: Pups (suckers) from the base: separate with roots when knee-high and pot up.

species.waterHowTo: Regular water in cool weather; they're shallow-rooted and wilt fast in containers. Fade and sulk in summer heat no matter what.
species.light: Full sun in spring/fall; part shade extends them into warm weather.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength every few weeks keeps blooms coming.
commonMistakes: Expecting summer bloom — they're cool-season flowers
Skipping deadheading
species.propagation: Seed in late summer (for fall/spring bloom) — chill seeds a week in the fridge first.

species.waterHowTo: Water at the base when the top few centimeters dry; wet foliage invites rust.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed once buds appear, then every 3 weeks.
commonMistakes: Not pinching young plants (pinch at 10cm for triple the spikes)
Letting spikes go to seed instead of cutting
species.propagation: Tiny seed on the soil surface (needs light); self-sows politely in mild gardens.

species.waterHowTo: Almost neglect-proof once up: water young plants, then only in real drought. Rich, wet soil = all ferny leaves, no flowers.
species.fertilizer: None — feeding backfires spectacularly.
commonMistakes: Fertilizing (foliage explosion, flower famine)
Coddling it — poor soil makes the best show
species.propagation: Direct-sow after frost; it self-sows generously for next year.

species.waterHowTo: No water until sprouts show (tubers rot in cold wet soil), then deep soaks 2-3× a week in bloom. Stop after frost kills the tops.
species.fertilizer: Low-nitrogen bloom feed every 3 weeks from budding.
commonMistakes: Watering freshly planted tubers
In cold climates: leaving tubers in the ground — lift and store them frost-free after the first freeze
species.propagation: Divide tuber clumps in spring — every division needs an 'eye' (growth bud) at the neck.

species.waterHowTo: Water well at fall planting, then leave them alone — winter moisture is enough. After bloom, let the foliage yellow completely (it recharges the bulb), then stop watering entirely for their summer dormancy.
species.fertilizer: Bulb feed or bone meal at planting; nothing else needed.
commonMistakes: Cutting or braiding the leaves after bloom — the bulb starves
Summer irrigation rotting dormant bulbs
species.propagation: Dig clumps after foliage dies, split off the daughter bulbs, replant the big ones in fall (small ones take 2-3 years to bloom).

species.waterHowTo: Rain usually covers them; water in dry springs while leaves are green. Foliage must die back naturally — then bone dry all summer.
species.fertilizer: Bulb feed at planting and as shoots emerge; done.
commonMistakes: Mowing/tying the leaves early
Planting too shallow (3× bulb height deep)
species.propagation: Lift and divide crowded clumps as foliage fades; replant offsets immediately or store dry until fall.

species.waterHowTo: Deep drink weekly in spring and after flowering; established peonies are drought-tolerant heirlooms that outlive their gardeners.
species.light: Full sun (6+ hours) for the big bloom show.
species.fertilizer: Light low-nitrogen feed after bloom; overfed peonies stop flowering.
commonMistakes: Planting the crown deeper than 5cm — the #1 cause of 'never blooms'
Moving them (they hate it; can sulk for 2 years)
species.propagation: Divide in FALL only: dig the crown, cut into pieces with 3-5 eyes each, replant shallow.

species.waterHowTo: Water to establish the first season; after that it's a prairie native that handles drought better than your lawn.
species.fertilizer: None needed in decent soil.
commonMistakes: Rich soil + fertilizer = floppy stems
Deadheading everything — leave fall seed heads for the goldfinches
species.propagation: Division in spring or fall every 3-4 years; also self-sows.

species.waterHowTo: Establish with regular water, then mostly rain-fed; droops dramatically in drought but bounces back with one soak.
species.fertilizer: None — tough prairie stock.
commonMistakes: Crowding without airflow (powdery mildew)
Overwatering established clumps
species.propagation: Division in spring, or let it self-sow — it's enthusiastic about it.

species.waterHowTo: Fall pots dry out daily in bloom — check every day. Garden plants: 2-3cm a week at the base; wet leaves invite disease.
species.fertilizer: Balanced feed spring-July, then stop (late feeding delays bloom).
commonMistakes: Letting store-bought pots wilt even once (they rarely fully recover)
Not pinching garden mums before July for bushiness
species.propagation: Spring tip cuttings root in 2-3 weeks, or divide woody clumps every couple of years.

species.waterHowTo: The shade-pot classic wilts theatrically the moment it's thirsty — daily checks in summer containers; revives fast after a drink.
species.light: Shade to part shade; sun scorches it.
species.fertilizer: Half-strength every 2-3 weeks all season.
commonMistakes: Full sun placement
Letting baskets dry to crisp even once
species.propagation: Soft tip cuttings root in a glass of water in about a week — among the easiest of all flowers.
